in_arabic.name: ظهي
in_arabic.long_meaning: شاديد النور، وهو الذي يبقي الشيء يبسط فيه النور. أو ما يقنعه الظلام على شيء منه. بل هو الذي يشفف الشيء من الظلام ويضع النور عليه.

in_urdu.name: ظہی
in_urdu.long_meaning: شادید مناظر ہوں، وہ دوسرے ساتھ رہتا ہوا اور شیء کو اس سے نہ سکتا ہوا کہ وہ بہترین نور کے لئے رہا ہوا، بلکہ بوجود ظلام کے ساتھ رہا ہوا اور وہ شیء سے بہترین نور دہانا ہوا.

in_hindi.name: ढाही
in_hindi.long_meaning: प्रकाशित होना, जिसमें शय्य के साथ झूठी ओछिपती ओर होना बhi अलग रहता होना और श्याम के साथ प्रकाशित रहना होना।

in_pashto.name: ظهي
in_pashto.long_meaning: نوری هوم، وه دوسرے ساتھ رہتا وہا اور شیء سے نور بھيجا رہتا هوا.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zahi holds great cultural significance as it conveys a sense of being fortunate or blessed, having been given a precious or valuable gift. It carries a positive and optimistic outlook, suggesting that the bearer of this name is valued and loved.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Zahi represents the blessing of being created by Allah, the supreme giver. It is a reminder that every gift, be it physical or intangible, comes from Allah and is a manifestation of His infinite mercy. The name also symbolizes the belief that every individual has inherent worth and value, making them a precious gift to the world.

historical_references.context: Zahi ibn Muhammad ibn Rushd, known in the Western world as Averroes, was an Andalusian philosopher, physician, and writer who lived from 1126 to 1198 AD. He is best known for his commentaries on Aristotle's works, and is considered to be the last major philosopher of the Islamic Golden Age.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that The life and works of Ibn Battuta by Ibn Battuta and Rodinson, page 143 The name Zahi carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Zahi, or Zaeh, was a famous Arab traveler who embarked on a pilgrimage to Mecca in 1325 AD and traveled extensively through North Africa, the Middle East, India, Central Asia, China, and Southeast Asia. He wrote an extensive travelogue detailing his experiences, which is an invaluable source of information about the world during that period.
